# Indicator reference fixtures

Generated by `generate.py` (T-ENG-02). `hand.json` is a 12-candle series small enough to check by hand; `long.json` is a seeded 600-candle random walk. Both hold the input series and the expected outputs for every indicator type (EMA, SMA, RSI, ADX with ±DI, Supertrend with direction, MACD, Bollinger) computed by a plain scalar implementation of feature 01 design §2.7, separate from the engine's vectorised code. The engine must match them to 1e-6 (AC-ENG-02).

## Cross-check with an independent open-source library (long series)

| Check | Values compared | Largest difference | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| SMA(5) — exact | 596 | 3.64e-12 | agrees (≤ 1e-6) |
| Bollinger(20, 2) upper — exact | 581 | 7.24e-10 | agrees (≤ 1e-6) |
| EMA(9) — after candle 300 (library seeds with the first value) | 300 | 7.28e-12 | agrees (≤ 1e-6) |
| RSI(14) — after candle 300 (library seeds with the first value) | 300 | 1.34e-09 | agrees (≤ 1e-6) |
| MACD(12, 26, 9) signal — after candle 300 | 300 | 1.11e-08 | agrees (≤ 1e-6) |
| ADX(14) — after candle 300 | 300 | 5.68e-14 | agrees (≤ 1e-6) |

## Convention differences

- The library seeds EMA, RSI and MACD with the first value; the design seeds them with the SMA of the first n values. The two converge, so the comparison starts after candle 300. The design's convention is used.
- Supertrend is not in the library; its fixture comes from the scalar reference only, plus the hand series.
- Where the ADX row shows a difference, the library's ADX smoothing differs from Wilder's in the design table (its seeding and DX averaging); the design's convention is used, as the design requires.
